expectations.text: Explains ISM applicability markings correctly: controls are marked for applicability by classification (OFFICIAL / OFFICIAL: Sensitive / PROTECTED / SECRET / TOP SECRET), and an OFFICIAL: Sensitive system implements the controls marked applicable at that level (with 'All'-marked controls included)
expectations.evidence: States 'Many ISM controls are marked as applicable to "All classifications" — these apply regardless... Others are specifically scoped to PROTECTED and above... those do not apply to your OFFICIAL: Sensitive system.' Conveys the correct core concept even though exact marking codes (P/S/TS) are only loosely referenced.

expectations.text: Describes the authorisation pathway as a define → select → implement → assess → authorise → monitor lifecycle, ending with an Authorising Official making a risk-based authorisation decision before go-live and ongoing monitoring after
expectations.evidence: Pathway steps are present (define SSP, implement, assess, SAR, risk acceptance/ATO, ongoing assurance) but the authorisation decision is attributed to 'the system owner or accountable authority (or delegate, often the CISO/agency head)' — the term 'Authorising Official' never appears, misattributing the risk-acceptance decision.

expectations.text: Names the core authorisation artefacts: a System Security Plan (with its control-implementation annex/matrix), documented security risk assessment, and incident response planning evidence
expectations.evidence: Names 'system security plan (SSP)... with the ISM controls selected', 'a security risk management plan/framework tailored to the system', and 'incident response plan' / 'Data spill and incident response — procedures for responding to and reporting cyber security incidents'.

expectations.text: Addresses the cloud dimension: using an IRAP-assessed cloud provider (consuming its assessment report), documenting the shared responsibility split between CSP and agency, and covering data sovereignty/residency considerations
expectations.evidence: Explicitly lists 'CSP certification, shared responsibility, data sovereignty, and use of the Information Security Registered Assessors Program (IRAP) assessed cloud services list' and later 'verifying the CSP holds an IRAP assessment or equivalent certification appropriate to OFFICIAL: Sensitive workloads' — covers all three required sub-elements.

expectations.text: Demonstrates release-awareness: states or reflects that the ISM is updated quarterly with June 2026 as the current release (e.g., ISM-XXXX control ID format, or an explicit release citation) — no invented control numbers
expectations.evidence: Only states 'ACSC updates it periodically' — never states quarterly cadence, never cites June 2026 as the current release, and instructs the reader to 'verify current chapter numbering and control IDs' rather than demonstrating actual release awareness.
